correctness.rationale: Every mixed allowed face has at most two vertices from each bipartition class and lies in one tetrahedron on matched index pairs. Both Δ(A)∪Z and Δ(B)∪Z collapse by dominated vertices to full simplices; their intersection Z collapses to the complete graph K_n as a 1-complex. Mayer–Vietoris and the homotopy pushout give a suspension, hence exactly choose(n-1,2) integral two-spheres. Under S_n the cycle module of the complete graph is ∧²ker(sum); the bipartition exchange is contiguous to the identity on Z but swaps the cover pieces and hence acts by minus one on H₂. Direct code checks both independent face predicates and every signed Lefschetz character for \(n=3\),4,5,6, with no extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The 2015 path/cycle/forest devoid-complex formulas cover the six-cycle special case but not the full matching-deleted bipartite family. The 2017 exact-crown paper covers ordinary independence (parameter one); its result cannot imply the higher-independence homotopy or integral symmetry action. The 2020 complete-multipartite theorem covers the undeleted \(K_{n,n}\), with homology in degree one, not the crown graph. Searches of aliases, published calculations, an indexed research corpus, and accessible earlier claims did not reveal the uniform topological and equivariant statement. This is best-knowledge originality, not publication-priority certification.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the natural bipartite double covers of complete graphs and arise by deleting one perfect matching from \(K_{n,n}\). The complete-bipartite two-independence complex has reduced homology concentrated in degree one, with n²-1 circle summands; matching deletion moves all reduced homology to degree two for the entire infinite crown family. The natural full \(\mathfrak S_n\times C_2\) integral module detects the effect of swapping bipartition classes and is not determined by Betti numbers. This is a motivated infinite-family structural classification, not a one-off enumeration or relabeling.
